name: DOUBLE DOOR AUTOCLAVE
desc: Triple-Walled Horizontal Pass-Through Double Door Autoclave Sterilizer engineered for absolute bio-containment and sterile item transfer between cleanroom zones. Features a spacious 432-liter rectangular sterilization chamber and advanced digital controls.
principle: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS DOUBLE DOOR AUTOCLAVE operates on the principle of saturated steam sterilization under elevated pressure, utilizing a triple-walled rectangular pressure vessel to achieve rapid and uniform thermal penetration. Within the 432-liter chamber, steam generated by industrial-grade immersion flange heating elements displaces ambient air, raising the internal temperature to a validated 121°C at a controlled pressure envelope of 15–20 psi. This moist-heat environment irreversibly denatures microbial proteins, nucleic acids, and enzymatic structures, achieving a sterility assurance level (SAL) of 10⁻⁶ for biohazardous waste, culture media, surgical instruments, and pharmaceutical glassware. The pass-through double-door configuration maintains absolute physical separation between contaminated and clean zones, preventing cross-contamination in BSL-2/3 facilities, vaccine production hubs, and cleanroom environments. The microprocessor-based PID controller continuously modulates heating element duty cycles and steam release via a vacuum breaker and steam trap, ensuring stable thermal equilibrium. Compliance with ISO 17665 and ASTM E1766 standards is supported by calibrated brass safety valves, an automated water level cut-off, and a digital timer with audio alarm for cycle completion. This instrument is essential for sterilizing strong acid-neutralized biological waste, volatile organic compound (VOC)-laden media, and heat-stable laboratory consumables used by doctors, B.Sc/M.Sc students, PhD researchers, and chemists in microbiology, pathology, and pharmaceutical quality control.
sop: Ensure both doors are closed and the chamber is empty before starting; verify the water level through the viewing glass and top up with distilled water if below the minimum mark.
Load items to be sterilized into the chamber through the 'contaminated' side door, arranging them loosely to allow steam circulation; close and lock the door securely.
Switch ON the main power supply and turn the autoclave power switch to the 'ON' position.
Press the 'SET' button once on the digital temperature controller to enter setpoint mode.
Use the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrows to adjust the target temperature to 121°C.
Press 'SET' again to lock the value; the controller will now display the current chamber temperature and begin heating.
Set the sterilization timer to the required holding time (typically 15–20 minutes for liquids, 30–60 minutes for solid waste) using the integrated digital timer.
Monitor the pressure gauge; ensure the pressure stabilizes between 15 psi and 20 psi during the holding phase.
At cycle completion, the audio alarm buzzer will sound; switch OFF the heating and allow the pressure to drop naturally to 0 psi before opening any door.
Open the 'clean' side door only after pressure is fully released and temperature is below 80°C; remove sterilized items using heat-resistant gloves.
Close both doors, switch OFF the main power, and record the cycle parameters in the autoclave logbook.

SAFETY WARNING: Never attempt to open either door while the chamber is pressurized or above 100°C; sudden steam release can cause severe burns. Always verify the pressure gauge reads 0 psi and the temperature display is below 80°C before unlocking any door. Do not sterilize sealed volatile solvents or strong oxidizing acids without validated venting protocols, as explosive pressure buildup may occur.
